document.abstract: This paper presents a preliminary study aiming to define a nonlinear model of a high-density optical disk readout process based on the Volterra series. Because of the high linear density and reduced track pitch, the signal readout is not a linear process. To cope with such a delicate problem, the identification of a suitable nonlinear model is required. In accordance with the Hopkins analysis, a physical model based on the optical scalar theory was implemented. The result of this analysis was then used to build a nonlinear analytical model based on the Volterra series. Some encouraging results from the preliminary draft model are presented here.

authors.bio: Luigi Agarossi received a degree in electronic engineering from the University of Bologna in 1981. He started working as a researcher in the GTE Telecommunication Radio Link R&D Dept., within the area of baseband and IF signal processing. In 1987, he joined Philips Research Monza, where he has been working on storage systems and architecture. Agarossi has participated in many European projects and is now involved with the SMASH (AC018) project as a group leader. In collaboration with the University of Bologna, he is also involved in some basic theoretical studies related to optical channel modeling and detection in the area of high-density optical storage.
authors.name: L. Agarossi

authors.bio: Sandro Bellini received a degree in electronic engineering from the Politecnico di Milano, Italy, in 1971. After his military service, he became a research engineer at the Space Telecommunications Center of CNR (National Research Council). He is now a full professor of electrical communications at the Politecnico di Milano. His main interests have been in narrow band (analog and digital) pulse modulation schemes, random access channels, continuous phase modulation, efficient simulation of digital transmission systems, and digital signal processing for various applications. Currently he is involved with coding for mobile satellite communications and digital recording of data. Bellini is a member of the IEEE and AEI.
authors.name: S. Bellini

authors.bio: Carlo Beoni received the Dr. Ing. degree in electronic engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1995. He received an Information Technology Master from Cefriel in 1996. Beoni has published papers on the optical amplifier pump laser and optical disk readout system. At present he is working on transmission equipment development and DSP application in the R&D department at Selta, Roveleto di Cadeo, Piacenza, Italy.
authors.name: C. Beoni

authors.bio: Pierangelo Migliorati received a degree in electronic engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1988 and a Masters in Information Technology from the Cefriel Research Center in Milan in 1989. From 1990 to 1993 he was involved in activities concerning image processing and coding at Cefriel. He also dealt with research activities in the areas of multimedia communications and medical image processing. From 1993 to 1995 Migliorati was involved in solving problems related to transmission and recording of digital TV signals. He is now an assistant professor at the University of Brescia, in the area of electrical communications and digital signal processing and is interested in activities related to channel equalization and motion estimation in image sequences.
authors.name: P. Migliorati
